<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

  /* Reading mode hides the chrome and the empty .arxiv-html-header marker: the pinned JS reads
     the marker's display to know which way to toggle. The marker draws no box. */
  .arxiv-html-header { display: contents; }
  html[data-reading-mode="enabled"] :is(.arxiv-html-site-chrome, .arxiv-html-header, .ds-site-footer) { display: none; }
  /* The paper controls' icons are blocks, so they sit centred (the pinned JS shows the theme
     icon by making its span a block). */
  .arxiv-html-site-chrome .ds-site-header-tools svg { display: block; width: 18px; height: 18px; flex-shrink: 0; fill: currentColor; }
  /* ar5iv dims every image in dark mode and puts it on a white wash, for paper figures;
     arXiv's own render as they are (the logo on the bar, the funder logos on their white
     chips). Important: ar5iv's dark rules are unlayered, as specific as
     :root:not([data-theme]) img:not(.ltx_no_dark_filter). */
  :is(.ds-site-header, .ds-site-footer) img { filter: none !important; }
  .ds-site-header img { background-color: transparent !important; }

  /* Wide (the theme's 1280px): the theme lays the body out as a grid whose full-width top rows
     were the band's and its sticky reader bar's. The band takes the first and scrolls away; the
     header, the paper's bar (no site navigation, the paper's controls), takes the second and
     stays in view, the one sticky bar, with the anchor clearance that requires (DESIGN-POLICIES).
     The controls show their names. */
  @media (min-width: 1280px) {
    html { scroll-padding-top: 80px; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome { display: contents; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > #ds-announcement { grid-area: announce; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome > .ds-site-header { grid-area: header; position: sticky; top: 0; z-index: 3; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-icon { display: none; }
  }
  /* Narrow: the header scrolls away, and the controls show icons (names kept for screen
     readers; Why HTML? goes). The theme's contents panel is fixed below where its old sticky
     bar was, and hidden only once the reader has closed it, so until then it is an invisible box
     over the header and the paper: it shows only while open, under the chrome, in its place in
     the page. The paper's footer (build logs, reporting instructions) keeps the text's side
     inset; the theme gives it none, so it met the screen edges. */
  @media (max-width: 1279px) {
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-wide { display: none; }
    .arxiv-html-site-chrome .tool-label { position: absolute; width: 1px; height: 1px; overflow: hidden; clip: rect(0 0 0 0); white-space: nowrap; }
    html:not([data-toc-display="block"]) .ltx_page_navbar { display: none; }
    .ltx_page_navbar { position: absolute; top: auto; }
    .arxiv-html-footer { padding-inline: 1rem; }
  }

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">The design of attention mechanisms in long-context large language models faces an “impossible triangle” among KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) achieves strong quality but incurs high KV cache overhead; alternative approaches such as Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) and Multi-matrix Factorization Attention (MFA) can compress the cache, but MLA suffers from quality loss while MFA substantially increases training and prefill compute.
We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix applies a near-identity transformation to queries within each KV group to recover virtual head diversity from halved physical query heads, and Linear Postmix fuses inter-head features via a low-rank <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I+AB^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I+AB^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> residual structure.
Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be folded into the query projection and Postmix into the output projection at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations. With only two KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during decoding.
Across four scales (0.6B, 1.7B, 4B dense, and 8B-A1B MoE) with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale (<math id="abstract1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.05% to <math id="abstract1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.81%), while reducing KV cache by <math id="abstract1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> vs. GQA-8 at dense scales and <math id="abstract1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> vs. GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9% (1.7B, <math id="abstract1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{=}4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{=}4096</annotation></semantics></math>).
On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by <math id="abstract1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.70 / <math id="abstract1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>2.60 % on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite; in a separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison after long-context mid-training, VHA attains an average RULER score of 84.4 over 8K–128K versus 73.0 for GQA, while using two rather than four KV heads in the full-attention layers. The source code is available at <a href="https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/VHA" title="" class="ltx_ref ltx_url ltx_font_typewriter">https://github.com/PaddlePaddle/VHA</a>.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Large language models are rapidly scaling toward longer contexts, with context windows expanding from 2K tokens to 128K and beyond <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Grattafiori et al., 2024</a>; <a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. As sequence lengths grow, the attention mechanism <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vaswani et al., 2017</a>)</cite> becomes a central efficiency bottleneck in both inference and training. During inference, the key-value (KV) cache grows linearly with sequence length, consuming substantial GPU memory and constraining both serving concurrency and generation latency. During training and prefill, the FLOPs of attention computation scale quadratically with sequence length. Since the design of the attention mechanism jointly determines KV cache size, computational cost, and model expressiveness, it is a critical factor governing the overall efficiency and quality of large language models.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The design of existing attention mechanisms faces three mutually constraining objectives, forming an “impossible triangle”: KV cache size, training and prefill FLOPs, and model quality. Consider the widely adopted Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ainslie et al., 2023</a>)</cite>: GQA with 8 KV heads (GQA-8) achieves strong quality, but incurs a KV cache of 4 KB per layer per token (in BF16). Directly reducing the number of KV heads to 2 (GQA-2) compresses the cache to 1 KB, but dramatically enlarges the group size so that far more query heads must share the same key-value pairs, causing attention diversity to drop sharply and resulting in a 1.00% quality degradation at the 1.7B scale. Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite> applies low-rank compression to reduce KV cache to 1.12 KB, but yields the lowest quality across multiple model scales. Multi-matrix Factorization Attention (MFA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> reduces the cache to 1 KB by enlarging the head dimension, achieving quality close to GQA-8, but at the cost of a 49.8% increase in training and prefill FLOPs (1.7B, <math id="S1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{=}4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{=}4096</annotation></semantics></math>). No existing approach achieves a satisfactory balance across all three dimensions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">We propose Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which simultaneously improves all three vertices of the impossible triangle through two lightweight linear operations. The core idea of VHA is to halve the number of physical query heads while setting the number of KV heads to only 2. Q Premix then applies a near-identity linear transformation to queries within each KV group, expanding the reduced physical query heads into virtual query heads to recover attention diversity. Linear Postmix applies a low-rank identity-residual transformation (<math id="S1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I+AB^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I+AB^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}H_{q}^{\prime}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}H_{q}^{\prime}/2</annotation></semantics></math>, e.g., <math id="S1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}4</annotation></semantics></math> at 1.7B) on the attention output, fusing cross-group inter-head features. Since VHA introduces no nonlinear operations, Premix can be directly folded into the query projection matrix and Postmix into the output projection matrix at inference time, reducing the model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that reuses all existing GQA inference optimizations in mainstream serving frameworks such as vLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwon et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and SGLang <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. Moreover, with only 2 KV heads, the group size in large models readily reaches 64, fully exploiting Tensor Core parallelism during the decoding phase.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Across four model scales (0.6B, 1.7B, 4B dense, and 8B-A1B MoE) with 4K-context 50B-token pretraining, VHA consistently surpasses the standard GQA baseline at every scale (<math id="S1.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.05% to <math id="S1.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.81%), while reducing KV cache by <math id="S1.p4.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> vs. GQA-8 at dense scales and <math id="S1.p4.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> vs. GQA-4 at the MoE scale, and lowering training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9% (1.7B, <math id="S1.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{=}4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{=}4096</annotation></semantics></math>). On an industrial 30B-A3B MoE model trained on 500B tokens at 8K context, VHA outperforms both MLA and GQA-4 by <math id="S1.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.70 / <math id="S1.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>2.60 % on a 12-benchmark base-model evaluation suite, demonstrating scalability to industrial model scale. A separate matched 10B-A1B MoE comparison further extends this advantage to 128K context under more aggressive KV compression. Our main contributions are as follows:</p>
<ol id="S1.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S1.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We propose VHA, employing Q Premix and Linear Postmix, two lightweight linear operations that simultaneously reduce KV cache and training/prefill FLOPs while improving model quality.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">VHA uses only linear operations and can be fully absorbed into a standard GQA-2 model at inference time, reusing existing serving frameworks such as vLLM and SGLang with zero additional overhead.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Direct inspection of the trained Premix and Postmix matrices reveals two complementary structures (group-conditioned query specialization and structured low-rank cross-head communication) that jointly close the gap of the doubly-compressed configuration; component ablations confirm that neither module is sufficient on its own.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S1.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S1.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Comprehensive evaluations across five scales (0.6B to 30B-A3B MoE) against MHA, GQA, MFA, and MLA establish VHA as the best attention mechanism that is Pareto-optimal on KV cache, training/prefill FLOPs, and downstream quality simultaneously; matched long-context evaluations through 128K further validate this advantage under aggressive KV compression.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1 </span>KV Cache Efficient Attention</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Standard Multi-Head Attention (MHA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vaswani et al., 2017</a>)</cite> maintains independent key and value projections per head, causing the KV cache to grow linearly with the number of heads. Multi-Query Attention (MQA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shazeer, 2019</a>)</cite> shares a single KV head across all query heads, drastically reducing the cache at the cost of quality. Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ainslie et al., 2023</a>)</cite> interpolates between MHA and MQA by allowing multiple query heads to share a group of KV heads, and has been widely adopted in LLaMA 2/3 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib23" title="" class="ltx_ref">Touvron et al., 2023</a>; <a href="#bib.bib24" title="" class="ltx_ref">Grattafiori et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and Qwen2 <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib25" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Several recent designs further compress the KV cache. Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Liu et al., 2024</a>)</cite> projects KV into a shared low-rank latent space and absorbs the up-projection matrices into Q and O at inference, but requires custom kernels and a non-standard inference pipeline. Multi-matrix Factorization Attention (MFA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2025</a>)</cite> enlarges the head dimension while reducing the number of KV heads, preserving model capacity under a tight cache budget but substantially increasing training and prefill FLOPs. Tensor Product Attention (TPA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025</a>)</cite> decomposes QKV into context-dependent tensor products. Grouped-head Latent Attention (GTA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2025</a>)</cite> extends MLA’s global latent space to a group-wise design. Simulated Attention Score (SAS) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2025</a>)</cite> projects a small number of low-dimensional KV heads into higher-dimensional spaces to simulate more attention heads, an idea related to VHA’s virtual head expansion; however, SAS operates on the KV side whereas VHA virtualizes on the query side. Low-Rank Key-Value Attention (LRKV) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">O’Neill et al., 2026</a>)</cite> shares a full-rank KV basis across heads and restores head-specific flexibility through low-rank residuals, a form reminiscent of VHA’s Postmix (<math id="S2.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I+AB^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I+AB^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>); yet LRKV acts in KV space and its additional structure remains at inference time. Cross-Layer Attention (CLA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Brandon et al., 2024</a>)</cite> and YOCO <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Sun et al., 2024</a>)</cite> reduce memory by sharing or reusing KV caches across layers.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike all of the above, VHA employs a richer training-time parameterization that merges exactly back into standard GQA at deployment, requiring no custom kernels or specialized inference procedures.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2 </span>Inter-Head Communication and Virtual Heads</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Talking-Heads Attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shazeer et al., 2020</a>)</cite> applies learned linear projections across heads before and after softmax, pioneering inter-head communication. <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citet"><a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Cordonnier et al. (2020)</a></cite> analyze multi-head attention from a collaborative perspective, revealing substantial redundancy among heads. More recently, Explicit Multi-head Attention (MEA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Peng et al., 2026</a>)</cite> introduces a head-level linear composition module for explicit cross-head interaction, and Interleaved Head Attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Duvvuri et al., 2026</a>)</cite> interleaves head representations to enable information exchange. In contrast to these methods, VHA does not mix across heads in the attention weight space; instead, it virtualizes in the query space via Premix and fuses inter-head features in the output space via a low-rank Postmix, with all operations being strictly linear and fully absorbable at inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3 </span>Reparameterization</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">RepVGG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ding et al., 2021</a>)</cite> uses a multi-branch training architecture (<math id="S2.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="3{\times}3+1{\times}1+\text{identity}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mn>3</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo>+</mo><mtext>identity</mtext></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">3{\times}3+1{\times}1+\text{identity}</annotation></semantics></math>) that merges into a single convolution at inference, demonstrating that decoupled training-time parameterization provides implicit regularization at zero inference cost. LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> performs parameter-efficient fine-tuning via low-rank decomposition (<math id="S2.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W+BA" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>W</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>A</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W+BA</annotation></semantics></math>). VHA extends this reparameterization paradigm from a single weight matrix to the head dimension of attention: Premix structurally factorizes the per-virtual-head query projections (<math id="S2.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math>), while Postmix introduces a low-rank identity-residual mixing on the head axis (<math id="S2.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I+AB^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I+AB^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>). Both modules are mathematically equivalent in the forward pass to a standard GQA configuration, yet the decoupled parameterization yields distinct optimization dynamics during training and merges back into a standard GQA-2 architecture at inference with zero overhead.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Method: Virtual Head Attention</h2>

<figure id="S3.F1" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.17959v1/VHAall.svg" id="S3.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/215;" width="476" height="215"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span><span id="S3.F1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Overview of Virtual Head Attention.</span> (a) VHA improves the trade-off among KV cache size, training/prefill FLOPs, and model quality by combining Q Premix and Linear Postmix during training, while absorbing both linear modules into standard GQA projections at inference. (b) Schematic of the KV cache–FLOPs–quality impossible triangle faced by existing attention designs. (c) Method comparison at 1.7B and 4B scales, plotting KV cache size against training FLOPs, with bubble area proportional to 8-task average accuracy.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1 </span>Preliminaries</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ainslie et al., 2023</a>)</cite> partitions <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> query heads into <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math> groups, where heads within each group share a common key-value pair. Given input <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times h}</annotation></semantics></math>, GQA computes <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=XW_{Q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=XW_{Q}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="K=XW_{K}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>K</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>K</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">K=XW_{K}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=XW_{V}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>V</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=XW_{V}</annotation></semantics></math>, where <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{q}d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{q}d}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{kv}d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>K</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{K}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{kv}d}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{kv}d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>V</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{V}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{kv}d}</annotation></semantics></math>. Each query head attends to its group’s key-value pair via scaled dot-product attention <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Vaswani et al., 2017</a>)</cite>, and all head outputs are concatenated and projected by <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{q}d\times h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{q}d\times h}</annotation></semantics></math>. During inference, K and V are cached, consuming <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4H_{kv}d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4H_{kv}d</annotation></semantics></math> bytes per layer per token in BF16. Reducing <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math> compresses the cache but enlarges the group size <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G=H_{q}/H_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>G</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G=H_{q}/H_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math>, forcing more query heads to share the same key-value pair and degrading attention diversity.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2 </span>Overall Design</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">VHA halves the number of physical query heads while setting <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}=2</annotation></semantics></math>, then recovers model expressiveness through two lightweight linear operations. Specifically, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}^{\prime}=H_{q}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}^{\prime}=H_{q}/2</annotation></semantics></math> physical query heads and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}=2</annotation></semantics></math> KV heads yield <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}=H_{kv}\times H_{q}^{\prime}=H_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>=</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}=H_{kv}\times H_{q}^{\prime}=H_{q}</annotation></semantics></math> virtual heads (matching the original GQA query head count), with <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}</annotation></semantics></math> identical in size to the original GQA output projection. The resulting KV cache is <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4\times 2\times d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times 2\times d</annotation></semantics></math> bytes per layer per token, <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m7" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> smaller than GQA-8 at dense scales and <math id="S3.SS2.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> smaller than GQA-4 at MoE scales.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">On top of this configuration, VHA introduces <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Q Premix</span>, which expands <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> physical query heads into <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> virtual query heads to restore attention diversity, and <span id="S3.SS2.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Linear Postmix</span>, which applies a low-rank identity-residual transformation on the attention output to fuse inter-head features.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inference absorption principle.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">VHA uses only linear operations (no nonlinear activations), so that at inference time Premix can be folded into <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}</annotation></semantics></math> and Postmix into <math id="S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, reducing the entire model to a standard GQA-2 architecture that directly reuses all existing GQA optimizations in frameworks such as vLLM <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib20" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kwon et al., 2023</a>)</cite> and SGLang <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib21" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zheng et al., 2024</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3 </span>Q Premix: Virtual Query Head Expansion</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Q Premix applies a near-identity linear transformation to physical query heads within each KV group, expanding them into virtual query heads. For KV group <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\{1,\dots,H_{kv}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\{1,\dots,H_{kv}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, each physical query head <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times d}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,\dots,H_{q}^{\prime}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,\dots,H_{q}^{\prime}\}</annotation></semantics></math>, is transformed as:</p>
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{Q}_{i,g}=Q_{i}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}},\quad W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="1.167em">,</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{Q}_{i,g}=Q_{i}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}},\quad W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(1)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math> is a per-group transformation matrix. We initialize <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}=I+\alpha\cdot\epsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mi>ϵ</mi></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}=I+\alpha\cdot\epsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>ϵ</mi><mo>∼</mo><mrow><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒩</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><msup><mi>σ</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma^{2})</annotation></semantics></math>, with a small scaling factor <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>. This near-identity initialization ensures that virtual query heads start as slight perturbations of the physical query heads, preserving training stability at the early stage. As training progresses, each <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math> gradually deviates from the identity to produce increasingly diverse attention patterns across virtual heads. Through this operation, <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> physical query heads are expanded into <math id="S3.SS3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}=H_{kv}\times H_{q}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}=H_{kv}\times H_{q}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> virtual query heads.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Structured factorization view.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Premix is mathematically equivalent in the forward pass to a standard <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>-head GQA whose query projections are structurally factorized. Specifically, defining</p>
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}\;=\;W_{Q}^{(i)}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{h\times d}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}\;=\;W_{Q}^{(i)}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{h\times d},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(2)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">the entire Premix-then-attend computation reduces, for any input <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> and any parameter values, to</p>
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\tilde{Q}_{i,g}K_{g}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}\right)V_{g}\;=\;\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(X\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}K_{g}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}\right)V_{g}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mi>softmax</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mi>softmax</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo>/</mo><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\tilde{Q}_{i,g}K_{g}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}\right)V_{g}\;=\;\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(X\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}K_{g}^{\top}/\sqrt{d}\right)V_{g}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(3)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">Thus VHA is a standard GQA with <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}=H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}=H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> virtual query heads and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math> KV heads, where the per-virtual-head query projections are constrained to lie on the structured low-dimensional manifold <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Why this factorization is useful.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The structured parameterization brings two benefits over an unconstrained <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>-head GQA. First, it is parameter- and compute-efficient: the Q path uses <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}^{\prime}hd+H_{kv}d^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}^{\prime}hd+H_{kv}d^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> parameters and a comparable number of FLOPs, versus <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}hd" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}hd</annotation></semantics></math> for a fully decoupled <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>-head Q projection. At the 1.7B scale, this yields a roughly 50% reduction in Q-projection parameters and FLOPs (the primary source of VHA’s training-FLOPs reduction). Second, although the forward pass is algebraically equivalent to training a single <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}</annotation></semantics></math>, the gradients of <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math> are coupled across all groups and physical heads, yielding a different optimization landscape and providing implicit regularization analogous to LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and RepVGG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ding et al., 2021</a>)</cite> (see Appendix <a href="#A7" title="Appendix G Premix as Structured Factorization of Virtual-Head Query Projections ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">G</span></a> for a formal analysis).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inference-time absorption.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Once training is complete and parameters are frozen, for each virtual head <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(i,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(i,g)</annotation></semantics></math> we precompute <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}\cdot W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}\cdot W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math>, after which VHA reduces to a standard GQA-2 with <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> independent query projections and <math id="S3.SS3.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}=2</annotation></semantics></math> KV heads.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.4 </span>Linear Postmix: Low-Rank Identity-Residual Mixing</h3>

<div id="S3.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">While Premix restores virtual head diversity within each KV group, the outputs across different groups still lack cross-group information exchange. Linear Postmix addresses this through a low-rank identity-residual structure.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times H_{v}\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\in\mathbb{R}^{S\times H_{v}\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> denote the attention output. Postmix computes:</p>
<table id="S3.E4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y^{\prime}=Y+BA^{\top}Y=\left(I+BA^{\top}\right)Y" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y^{\prime}=Y+BA^{\top}Y=\left(I+BA^{\top}\right)Y</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(4)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times r}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> is the bottleneck rank (default <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=H_{q}^{\prime}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=H_{q}^{\prime}/2</annotation></semantics></math>, e.g., <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}4</annotation></semantics></math> at 1.7B). The operation acts along the head dimension independently for each token and head-dimension channel, applying the transformation <math id="S3.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I+BA^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times H_{v}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I+BA^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times H_{v}}</annotation></semantics></math> to the head axis.</p>
</div>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Initialization.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> is initialized with small random values and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> with zeros, ensuring <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="BA^{\top}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">BA^{\top}=0</annotation></semantics></math> at the start of training so that Postmix acts as the identity and does not disturb the initial training dynamics. As training progresses, <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> gradually learns effective cross-group mixing patterns.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Linear redundancy and reparameterization benefit.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Mathematically, Postmix can be absorbed into <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math>. Using the row-major Kronecker identity <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(MY)^{\top}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}(M^{\top}\otimes I_{d})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(MY)^{\top}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}(M^{\top}\otimes I_{d})</annotation></semantics></math> <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roger and Charles, 1994</a>)</cite>:</p>
<table id="S3.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\!\left((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\right)W_{O}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}W_{O}^{\prime}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\!\left((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\right)W_{O}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}W_{O}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)\,W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)\,W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}</annotation></semantics></math>. Thus, linear Postmix is theoretically redundant (see Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Proof of Postmix Linear Redundancy ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a> for the complete derivation). However, ablation experiments (Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>) show that adding Postmix on top of Premix yields a <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>1.19 % improvement at 1.7B, analogous to the implicit regularization observed in RepVGG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ding et al., 2021</a>)</cite> and the low-rank decomposition in LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>)</cite>: the separated gradient paths of <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> provide a different optimization landscape, while the low-rank constraint (<math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\ll H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>≪</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\ll H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>) acts as an additional regularizer preventing cross-head mixing from overfitting.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inference-time absorption.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At inference, we precompute <math id="S3.SS4.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, after which VHA reduces to standard GQA-2. Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ Appendix F VHA Algorithm ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> (Appendix <a href="#A6" title="Appendix F VHA Algorithm ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">F</span></a>) summarizes the complete training forward pass and the one-time inference-absorption procedure.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.5 </span>Efficiency Analysis</h3>

<section id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Training and prefill FLOPs.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">By halving the physical <math id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}</annotation></semantics></math>, VHA directly reduces Q projection FLOPs. The additional cost of Premix (<math id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}d^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}d^{2}</annotation></semantics></math>) and Postmix (<math id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="4H_{v}rd" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4H_{v}rd</annotation></semantics></math>) is negligible compared to the FLOPs saved by halving the Q projection. Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.5 Computational Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> quantifies this trade-off in detail across all four model scales (<math id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{=}4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{=}4096</annotation></semantics></math>); VHA emerges as the best Pareto-optimal point on KV cache and FLOPs at every scale (Section <a href="#S4.SS5" title="4.5 Computational Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.5</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Decoding inference.</h4>

<div id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Autoregressive decoding is memory-bound <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib22" title="" class="ltx_ref">Pope et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, so KV cache size directly governs latency and serving concurrency. With KV cache reduced by <math id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> vs. GQA-8 (dense) or <math id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> vs. GQA-4 (MoE), VHA achieves a corresponding 2–4<math id="S3.SS5.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>×</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\times</annotation></semantics></math> theoretical speedup in memory-bound decoding. Since Premix and Postmix are fully absorbed at inference, VHA’s decoding cost is identical to standard GQA-2.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.T1" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 1: </span><span id="S3.T1.11" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Pretraining accuracy across four model scales.</span>
We report zero-shot accuracy (%) on eight standard multiple-choice benchmarks.
<span id="S3.T1.12" class="ltx_text ltx_font_smallcaps">Cache</span> is KV cache per layer per token in BF16 (KB).
<span id="S3.T1.13" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bold</span> marks the best per scale per column; ties are bolded jointly.
VHA achieves the highest average accuracy at every scale while using the
smallest KV cache. Per-method full configurations and benchmark citations
are in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Training Configuration and Benchmark Citations ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>; per-method training-FLOPs comparison is in Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.5 Computational Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</figcaption>

<td id="S3.T1.14.1.19.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.2pt 2.8pt;"><span id="S3.T1.14.1.19.11.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">39.56</span></td>
<td id="S3.T1.14.1.19.12" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.2pt 2.8pt;"><span id="S3.T1.14.1.19.12.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">53.79</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S3.T1.14.1.20" class="ltx_tr">
