</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Experiments</h2>

<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Experimental Setup</h3>

<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Baselines.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We compare VHA with MHA, GQA, MFA, and MLA across all scales. Following common practice, GQA uses 8 KV heads at dense scales (0.6B/1.7B/4B) and 4 KV heads at MoE scales (8B-A1B and 30B-A3B). VHA halves the physical query heads relative to GQA and uses <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}{=}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}{=}2</annotation></semantics></math>, yielding <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> KV cache compression at dense scales and <math id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> at MoE scales.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Small-scale pretraining.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We pretrain Qwen3-architecture models at four scales (dense at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 4B parameters, plus an 8B-A1B MoE) on 50B tokens of FineWeb-Edu with BF16 mixed precision and a 4K context length. We report zero-shot accuracy on eight standard benchmarks.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Industrial-scale pretraining.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We pretrain an ERNIE-style 30B-A3B MoE on an internal multi-domain pretraining corpus (web text, books, code, and multilingual data) with FP8 mixed precision on 500B tokens at 8K context. We evaluate on 12 standard base-model benchmarks spanning general knowledge, math &amp; STEM, coding, and multilingual capabilities. Full model configurations, benchmark details, and training hyperparameters are in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Training Configuration and Benchmark Citations ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Long-context mid-training.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We additionally compare VHA and GQA on a matched MiMo-2.5-Flash-style 10B-A1B MoE backbone that interleaves full and sliding-window attention at a 1:3 ratio. The two models share the backbone, data, optimization, and sliding-window layers; only the full-attention layers differ, using two KV heads for VHA and four for GQA. We evaluate through 128K, with the stage-wise recipe and benchmark definitions reported in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Long-Context Evaluation ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2 </span>Main Results</h3>

<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Cross-scale consistency.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">VHA achieves the highest average accuracy at every scale, surpassing the GQA baseline by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.05% to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.81% while using the smallest KV cache: 1.00 KB per layer per token, tied with MFA, <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="4\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">4\times</annotation></semantics></math> smaller than GQA-8 at dense scales and <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="2\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2\times</annotation></semantics></math> smaller than GQA-4 at the MoE scale. The advantage holds across both dense and MoE architectures. A separate matched-harness study at 0.6B confirms the same ordering across repeated runs, with VHA reaching <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50.40{\pm}0.07" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50.40</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.07</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50.40{\pm}0.07</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}4" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}4</annotation></semantics></math>) versus GQA’s <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50.00{\pm}0.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>50.00</mn><mo>±</mo><mn>0.34</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50.00{\pm}0.34</annotation></semantics></math> (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n{=}3" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>3</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n{=}3</annotation></semantics></math>); full results are in Appendix <a href="#A2" title="Appendix B Additional Robustness Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">B</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Trade-offs against each baseline.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At equal KV cache (1.00 KB), VHA dominates MFA at every scale (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.10% to <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.77%) while reducing training and prefill FLOPs by 7.9%, compared with MFA’s <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>49.8% increase at the 1.7B scale (<math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{=}4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{=}4096</annotation></semantics></math>; Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.5 Computational Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>). Full-cache MHA falls below GQA-8 at every dense scale despite using a <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="\geq 1.5\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>1.5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\geq 1.5\times</annotation></semantics></math> larger cache, confirming that grouping the queries is essentially free. MLA underperforms at every scale, suggesting that latent KV compression is less effective than head-level virtualization at the 50B-token training budget used here. Per-method training loss curves at all four scales are reported in Appendix <a href="#A5" title="Appendix E Training Loss Curves ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">E</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S4.T2" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 2: </span><span id="S4.T2.7" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Recovering from a doubly-compressed shape (1.7B).</span>
GQA 16-8-8 is the standard GQA-8 baseline; GQA 16-2-2 reduces only <math id="S4.T2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math>
to obtain a 1 KB KV cache; GQA 8-2-2 additionally halves the physical query
heads to match VHA’s shape but lacks Premix and Postmix. <math id="S4.T2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> is the
gap to the GQA 16-8-8 baseline.</figcaption>

<th id="S4.T2.8.1.1.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.2pt 3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.8.1.1.10.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:70%;">SIQA</span></th>
<th id="S4.T2.8.1.1.11" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_th ltx_th_column ltx_border_tt" style="padding:0.2pt 3.0pt;"><span id="S4.T2.8.1.1.11.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:70%;">Avg</span></th>

</thead>
<tbody class="ltx_tbody">

</section>
<section id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Recovering from a doubly-compressed shape.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reducing GQA’s KV head count from 8 to 2 (GQA 16-2-2) costs <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>1.00% in average accuracy at the 1.7B scale; further halving the physical query heads to match VHA’s shape (GQA 8-2-2) costs another <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>0.71%, totaling <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>1.71% vs. the GQA-8 baseline. With the same (8, 2, 2) shape, VHA recovers all of this loss and exceeds the original baseline by <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.41%, despite using only 25% of GQA-8’s KV cache and 50% of its physical query heads. The doubly-compressed (8, 2, 2) shape that on its own forfeits <math id="S4.SS2.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>1.71% thus becomes a winning configuration once Premix and Postmix are introduced.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>

<span id="S4.T3.15" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bold</span> marks the best per column.

<td id="S4.T3.16.3.7" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.2pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.16.3.7.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">45.20</span></td>
<td id="S4.T3.16.3.8" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center" style="padding:0.2pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.16.3.8.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">49.66</span></td></tr>
<tr id="S4.T3.16.4" class="ltx_tr">
<th id="S4.T3.16.4.1" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.2pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.16.4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">VHA</span></th>
<th id="S4.T3.16.4.2" class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_th ltx_th_row ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.2pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.16.4.2.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">24-2-2</span></th>
<td id="S4.T3.16.4.3" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.2pt 4.0pt;"><span id="S4.T3.16.4.3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold" style="font-size:80%;">1.00</span></td>

</tbody>
</table>
</figure>
<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At the 30B-A3B MoE scale (500B tokens; FP8 mixed precision; full setup in Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Training Configuration and Benchmark Citations ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>), Table <a href="#S4.T3" title="Table 3 ‣ 4.3 Large-scale and long-context validation ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> shows that VHA 24-2-2 attains the highest 12-benchmark average while using only 50% of GQA-4’s KV cache and 89% of MLA’s, confirming that the trends observed at 0.6B<math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>8B-A1B carry over to the production-scale MoE regime. The category-level breakdown shows that gains are broadly distributed: General <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>3.39 / <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.68%, Math &amp; STEM <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>3.31 / <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>2.91%, Coding <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>1.38 / <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>1.14%, Multilingual <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>2.30 / <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.36% (VHA vs. GQA / MLA), indicating head-level virtualization scales gracefully across heterogeneous downstream tasks. Per-benchmark scores for all 12 evaluations are in Appendix <a href="#A3" title="Appendix C Per-benchmark Scores for the 30B-A3B MoE Evaluation ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">C</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Long-context validation.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">At the final 128K checkpoint, VHA outperforms the matched GQA baseline on RULER at every evaluated length from 8K to 128K, with a length-average of 84.4 versus 73.0 (<math id="S4.SS3.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>11.4 points). The advantage extends to complementary evaluations at 128K: VHA outperforms GQA on LongBench-v2 (24.2 vs. 18.9) and BABILong (38.2 vs. 31.1), while remaining on par on InfiniteBench (31.5 vs. 31.8); averaged across lengths, VHA wins, ties, and loses 3/1/1 HELMET categories. Together, these results demonstrate that VHA preserves its quality advantage through 128K while halving the KV heads and KV cache of the full-attention layers relative to GQA-4; complete results are in Appendix <a href="#A1" title="Appendix A Long-Context Evaluation ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">A</span></a>.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Ablations</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We ablate VHA’s design choices at the 1.7B scale (additionally at 4B for the component contribution), isolating (i) the contribution of Premix and Postmix, (ii) the Postmix rank, and (iii) whether non-linearity helps either module.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Reading the <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta</annotation></semantics></math> column of Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> (left and middle), the two modules address complementary deficits of the doubly-compressed shape: only their joint VHA configuration consistently achieves the largest gains at both scales at <math id="S4.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> of GQA-8’s KV cache; we provide a mechanistic interpretation of this complementarity in Section <a href="#S5" title="5 Analysis: How VHA Reparameterization Works ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a>.</p>
</div>

</figure>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Postmix rank.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">With Premix fixed at the 1.7B scale, sweeping the Postmix rank gives Avg <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="54.50/54.24/54.15" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>54.50</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>54.24</mn><mo>/</mo><mn>54.15</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">54.50/54.24/54.15</annotation></semantics></math> for <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\in\{4,32,128\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>32</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\in\{4,32,128\}</annotation></semantics></math>: larger <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>r</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r</annotation></semantics></math> monotonically lowers training loss but degrades downstream evaluation, indicating that the low-rank constraint provides useful implicit regularization. We therefore fix <math id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r=H_{q}^{\prime}/2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>/</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r=H_{q}^{\prime}/2</annotation></semantics></math> across all scales (Section <a href="#S3.SS4" title="3.4 Linear Postmix: Low-Rank Identity-Residual Mixing ‣ 3 Method: Virtual Head Attention ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a> / Appendix <a href="#A4" title="Appendix D Training Configuration and Benchmark Citations ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">D</span></a>).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Activation.</h4>

<div id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Replacing the linear formulation with SiLU on either or both modules consistently degrades quality at 1.7B (Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a>, right), regardless of where the non-linearity is inserted. Beyond the empirical loss, every non-linear variant forfeits inference-time absorption: with both modules linear the entire VHA computation collapses to standard GQA-2 at serving time, whereas any non-linearity must remain in the runtime kernel. We therefore keep both modules strictly linear, simultaneously achieving the highest empirical quality and lossless absorption into standard GQA-2 at inference.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.5 </span>Computational Efficiency</h3>

<figure id="S4.T5" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 5: </span><span id="S4.T5.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Computational efficiency across four model scales</span> (<math id="S4.T5.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S{=}4096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>S</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>4096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S{=}4096</annotation></semantics></math>).
For each scale we list per-method query/key/value head counts, KV cache
per layer per token (BF16, KB), training FLOPs per token aggregated over
all transformer layers (G), and the relative change vs. the per-scale
GQA baseline (GQA-8 dense, GQA-4 MoE). <span id="S4.T5.5" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bold</span> highlights VHA, the method that achieves the best joint KV cache<math id="S4.T5.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>FLOPs Pareto optimum at every
scale. MHA’s lower FLOPs at three scales reflect its smaller query head
count under our parameter-matched configurations (<math id="S4.T5.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}{=}12" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>12</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}{=}12</annotation></semantics></math> at 0.6B/1.7B,
<math id="S4.T5.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}{=}20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}{=}20</annotation></semantics></math> at 4B/8B-A1B versus GQA’s <math id="S4.T5.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}{=}16</annotation></semantics></math> or <math id="S4.T5.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}{=}32" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>32</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}{=}32</annotation></semantics></math>), at the
cost of a <math id="S4.T5.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.T5.m16" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="10\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\times</annotation></semantics></math> larger KV cache.</figcaption>

</figure>
<div id="S4.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T5" title="Table 5 ‣ 4.5 Computational Efficiency ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> quantifies the joint KV cache–FLOPs trade-off across the four model scales of Table <a href="#S3.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ Decoding inference. ‣ 3.5 Efficiency Analysis ‣ 3 Method: Virtual Head Attention ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a>. VHA is the only method that simultaneously matches the smallest KV cache (1.00 KB) and reduces training/prefill FLOPs below the per-scale GQA baseline (<math id="S4.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>8.1 / <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>7.9 / <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>7.6 / <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>6.5 % across scales). MFA matches the cache but pays a <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>48–74 % FLOPs penalty; MLA’s latent compression yields a slightly larger cache (1.12 KB) and raises FLOPs at three of four scales (up to <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>10.9 % at 8B-A1B). MHA appears competitive on FLOPs only because its smaller query head count under our parameter-matched configurations comes with a <math id="S4.SS5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>6</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6</annotation></semantics></math>–<math id="S4.SS5.p1.m8" class="ltx_math_unparsed" alttext="10\times" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>10</mn><mo lspace="0.222em">×</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10\times</annotation></semantics></math> larger KV cache. Combined with VHA’s complete inference absorption to standard GQA-2 (Section <a href="#S3.SS4" title="3.4 Linear Postmix: Low-Rank Identity-Residual Mixing ‣ 3 Method: Virtual Head Attention ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3.4</span></a>), this makes VHA the best Pareto-optimal point on the cache–FLOPs–quality triangle in our experiments.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Analysis: How VHA Reparameterization Works</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Beyond task accuracy, VHA should exploit the limited information available under aggressive KV sharing. We therefore inspect the Premix and Postmix matrices of trained VHA models (Premix on the 1.7B, Postmix on the 4B model), asking whether (i) Premix learns a group-conditioned query geometry, (ii) Postmix learns structured low-rank cross-head communication, and (iii) the two jointly close the doubly-compressed gap of Section <a href="#S4.SS4" title="4.4 Ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4.4</span></a>.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F2" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.17959v1/premix0503.svg" id="S5.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/113;" width="476" height="113"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2: </span><span id="S5.F2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Q Premix weight analysis on a trained Qwen-1.7B VHA model.</span>
(a) Per-layer Frobenius deviation <math id="S5.F2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}-I\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}-I\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> per KV group (group mean overlaid).
(b) Per-layer mean pairwise distance <math id="S5.F2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|W_{g_{1}}^{\mathrm{premix}}-W_{g_{2}}^{\mathrm{premix}}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|W_{g_{1}}^{\mathrm{premix}}-W_{g_{2}}^{\mathrm{premix}}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> between KV groups.</figcaption>
</figure>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Premix learns non-trivial, group-differentiated query transforms.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Premix introduces a learnable per-group query transform <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math> before RoPE, initialized near identity. Two trivial outcomes would falsify our hypothesis: (a) <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math> remains near identity after training, rendering the module a no-op; or (b) all KV groups converge to the same matrix, degenerating Premix into a group-agnostic shared adapter without group-conditioned specialization. Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5 Analysis: How VHA Reparameterization Works ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> refutes both: panel (a) shows that <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}-I\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><mi>I</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}-I\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> is substantially nonzero and most pronounced in mid-to-late layers (peak 5.85), and panel (b) shows that the inter-group distance <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\|W_{g_{1}}^{\mathrm{premix}}-W_{g_{2}}^{\mathrm{premix}}\|_{F}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo>−</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><msub><mi>g</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">‖</mo></mrow><mi>F</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\|W_{g_{1}}^{\mathrm{premix}}-W_{g_{2}}^{\mathrm{premix}}\|_{F}</annotation></semantics></math> is of comparable magnitude (peak 6.13), yielding a ratio well below the <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sqrt{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sqrt{2}</annotation></semantics></math> value expected under fully independent groups and far above the zero expected under a shared deviation. This quantifies that the two KV groups learn substantially but not independently different query transforms. Premix therefore learns differentiated query probing directions per KV group under a fixed minimal KV cache, realizing genuine group-conditioned virtual-head expansion rather than mere parameter augmentation.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F3" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.17959v1/postmix0505.svg" id="S5.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/126;" width="476" height="126"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 3: </span><span id="S5.F3.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Postmix head-mixing analysis on a trained Qwen-4B VHA model.</span>
Sankey diagrams of <math id="S5.F3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|AB^{\top}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|AB^{\top}|</annotation></semantics></math> across five representative layers, with ribbons flowing from source heads (left, colored by KV group) to recombined output heads (right); width and color saturation proportional to <math id="S5.F3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|AB^{\top}|_{j,i}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|AB^{\top}|_{j,i}</annotation></semantics></math>.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Postmix learns structured low-rank cross-head communication.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Postmix recombines the <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> attention output heads via the low-rank residual <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I+BA^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>I</mi><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I+BA^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>, where entry <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(j,i)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>j</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(j,i)</annotation></semantics></math> of <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|AB^{\top}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|AB^{\top}|</annotation></semantics></math> encodes the contribution of source head <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="j" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>j</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">j</annotation></semantics></math> to recombined head <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>. The central question is whether <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> merely performs a per-head rescaling (a strictly diagonal pattern) or genuinely redistributes information across heads (off-diagonal flow). Figure <a href="#S5.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Premix learns non-trivial, group-differentiated query transforms. ‣ 5 Analysis: How VHA Reparameterization Works ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> visualizes <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="|AB^{\top}|" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">|</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">|AB^{\top}|</annotation></semantics></math> for the trained 4B model and reveals pronounced off-diagonal flow, ruling out the trivial per-head-rescaling outcome. The dominant pattern is <em id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_emph ltx_font_italic">within-group</em> redistribution: Postmix primarily rebalances information among heads sharing the same KV cache, with a sparse but consistent set of cross-group bridges providing inter-group connectivity without additional KV heads.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Joint reparameterization closes the doubly-compressed gap.</h4>

<div id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Tying these analyses back to the component ablation in Table <a href="#S4.T4" title="Table 4 ‣ 4.4 Ablations ‣ 4 Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> clarifies the three numbers reported there. Premix-only retains the group-conditioned query geometry of Figure <a href="#S5.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 5 Analysis: How VHA Reparameterization Works ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> but lacks Postmix’s cross-group repair pathway, hence the <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>0.78% gap at 1.7B. Postmix-only owns the cross-head mixing channels of Figure <a href="#S5.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ Premix learns non-trivial, group-differentiated query transforms. ‣ 5 Analysis: How VHA Reparameterization Works ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> but operates over collapsed, unspecialized virtual heads, hence the <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>−</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-</annotation></semantics></math>0.14% gap. Only the joint configuration realizes both structures simultaneously, yielding a <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>+</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+</annotation></semantics></math>0.41% advantage over GQA-8 at <math id="S5.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="25\%" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>25</mn><mo>%</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">25\%</annotation></semantics></math> of its KV cache. VHA’s effectiveness therefore arises from the functional complementarity of its two modules: Premix and Postmix are not interchangeable, and neither suffices alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We have presented Virtual Head Attention (VHA), which mitigates the tension among KV cache size, training/prefill FLOPs, and model quality through two lightweight linear operations: Q Premix and Linear Postmix. By halving physical query heads and recovering expressiveness via virtual head expansion and low-rank cross-group mixing, VHA reduces the KV cache to its architectural minimum while simultaneously lowering training FLOPs and improving model quality. Since all added operations are strictly linear, VHA fully absorbs into standard GQA-2 at inference, reusing existing serving optimizations with zero additional overhead. Analysis of trained models reveals that Premix and Postmix are functionally complementary and neither suffices alone, explaining why the joint configuration consistently surpasses the GQA baseline across all five evaluated scales (0.6B to 30B-A3B MoE). A matched 10B-A1B evaluation further shows that VHA maintains this advantage over GQA through 128K context.</p>
</div>
</section>

<span class="ltx_bibblock"><span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_journal">Advances in neural information processing systems</span> <span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_volume">37</span>, <span class="ltx_text ltx_bib_pages">pp. 62557–62583</span>.
</span>
<span class="ltx_bibblock ltx_bib_cited">Cited by: <a href="#S1.p3.1" title="1 Introduction ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">§1</span></a>,
<a href="#S3.SS2.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" title="Inference absorption principle. ‣ 3.2 Overall Design ‣ 3 Method: Virtual Head Attention ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">§3.2</span></a>.
</span></li>

</section>
<div class="ltx_pagination ltx_role_newpage"></div>
<section id="Sx2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section">Limitations and Future Work</h2>

<div id="Sx2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Sx2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Our largest validation is at the 30B-A3B MoE scale trained on 500B tokens; scaling VHA to larger MoE models and substantially more training data (e.g., 20T tokens) remains an important direction. We further validate VHA through 128K on a 10B-A1B MoE, while broader long-context architectures and training recipes remain to be explored. VHA’s behavior under reinforcement learning training paradigms is also worth exploring. Finally, VHA is orthogonal to other KV cache compression techniques such as quantization and sparsification, and combining them may yield further inference savings.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix A </span>Long-Context Evaluation</h2>

<section id="A1.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.1 </span>Model and Stage-wise Training</h3>

<div id="A1.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct a controlled long-context comparison on a MiMo-2.5-Flash-style 10B-A1B MoE backbone that interleaves full and sliding-window attention at a 1:3 ratio. The GQA and VHA models share the same backbone, data, optimization settings, and sliding-window layers. They differ only in the full-attention layers: GQA uses four KV heads, whereas VHA uses two; all sliding-window layers use eight KV heads in both models. Thus, VHA halves the KV cache of the full-attention layers without changing the sliding-window component.</p>
</div>
<div id="A1.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The 8K pretraining stage uses 500B tokens and ends at 60K steps. Long-context mid-training then uses 100B tokens at 32K followed by another 100B tokens at 128K. These stages add 12K and 24K steps, yielding cumulative checkpoints at 72K and 96K steps, respectively. The RoPE base is increased from <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="10^{4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>4</mn></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">10^{4}</annotation></semantics></math> at 8K to <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="6.4{\times}10^{5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>6.4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">6.4{\times}10^{5}</annotation></semantics></math> at 32K and <math id="A1.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="5{\times}10^{6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>5</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">5{\times}10^{6}</annotation></semantics></math> at 128K. We report intermediate results from the 32K checkpoint and final results from the 128K checkpoint.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.2 </span>RULER and HELMET</h3>

<div id="A1.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate RULER and HELMET from 8K to 128K. RULER Overall is the mean over 13 tasks: eight Retrieval, two Aggregation, two QA, and one Variable Tracking task. HELMET is reported by category because its categories measure distinct capabilities.</p>
</div>

<div id="A1.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At the final checkpoint, VHA leads RULER Overall at every evaluated length, with an average of 84.4 across lengths versus 73.0 for GQA. The largest gap occurs in Variable Tracking, where VHA scores 92.6/87.2/83.0 at 32K/64K/128K versus 3.2/4.2/3.0 for GQA. HELMET is more heterogeneous: averaged across lengths, VHA wins RAG, LongQA, and Summarization, ties Reranking, and trails on ICL.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A1.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">A.3 </span>Complementary Long-Context Evaluations</h3>

<div id="A1.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A1.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We additionally report LongBench-v2, InfiniteBench, BABILong, a short-context eight-task average, and language-modeling bits per byte on the four ProLong domains. At the final checkpoint, VHA wins seven of the eight reported metrics; InfiniteBench is nearly tied.</p>
</div>

<section id="A2" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix B </span>Additional Robustness Experiments</h2>

<div id="A2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The following experiments use a more efficient training implementation than the main 50B-token runs. Absolute scores therefore need not match the main tables, but all methods within each comparison use the same implementation and training recipe.</p>
</div>
<section id="A2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.1 </span>Repeated-run Robustness at 0.6B</h3>

<div id="A2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We repeat the 0.6B experiment four times for VHA and three times for GQA. We report every run using zero-shot BF16 evaluation, with normalized accuracy used where available. Avg is the unweighted mean over eight tasks, and <math id="A2.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pm" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>±</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pm</annotation></semantics></math> denotes the sample standard deviation across run-level averages. VHA achieves a higher mean with lower observed dispersion.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A2.T8" class="ltx_table">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:70%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 8: </span>Repeated-run results at 0.6B (%). Every run is reported. Bold in the summary rows marks the higher across-run mean.</figcaption>

<td id="A2.T8.4.1.10.10" class="ltx_td ltx_align_center ltx_border_bb" style="padding:0.15pt 3.5pt;"><math id="A2.T8.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="50.00{\pm}0.34" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn mathsize="0.700em">50.00</mn><mo mathsize="0.700em">±</mo><mn mathsize="0.700em">0.34</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">50.00{\pm}0.34</annotation></semantics></math></td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
</span></div>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">B.2 </span>Sensitivity to Premix Initialization</h3>

<div id="A2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We train the 1.7B model from scratch with the same recipe while changing only the Premix initialization: the default near-identity initialization (<math id="A2.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha{=}0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha{=}0.1</annotation></semantics></math>), a larger identity-anchored perturbation (<math id="A2.SS2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha{=}1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1.0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha{=}1.0</annotation></semantics></math>), and fully random initialization without the identity anchor. All three runs remain stable, with no gradient explosion, divergence, NaN, or Inf. Their early loss and pre-clipping gradient norms are similar (Table <a href="#A2.T9" title="Table 9 ‣ B.2 Sensitivity to Premix Initialization ‣ Appendix B Additional Robustness Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a>), while the default near-identity initialization gives the highest downstream average (Table <a href="#A2.T10" title="Table 10 ‣ B.2 Sensitivity to Premix Initialization ‣ Appendix B Additional Robustness Experiments ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">10</span></a>).</p>
</div>

<section id="A4" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix D </span>Training Configuration and Benchmark Citations</h2>

<section id="A4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">D.1 </span>Model Architecture and Training Hyperparameters</h3>

<div id="A4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#A4.T12" title="Table 12 ‣ D.1 Model Architecture and Training Hyperparameters ‣ Appendix D Training Configuration and Benchmark Citations ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">12</span></a> lists the backbone architecture and training
hyperparameters for all five scales.
Small-scale models follow the Qwen3 architecture; the 30B-A3B model uses
an ERNIE-style MoE architecture with auxiliary-free routing
(<span id="A4.SS1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">noaux_tc</span>) and z-loss (<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\lambda{=}4{\times}10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>λ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\lambda{=}4{\times}10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>).
We use AdamW <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Loshchilov and Hutter, 2017</a>]</cite> with <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{1}{=}0.9" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.9</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{1}{=}0.9</annotation></semantics></math>,
<math id="A4.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\beta_{2}{=}0.95" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>β</mi><mn>2</mn></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>0.95</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\beta_{2}{=}0.95</annotation></semantics></math>, weight decay <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="0.1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>0.1</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">0.1</annotation></semantics></math>, and gradient clipping at <math id="A4.SS1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>

<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering" style="font-size:80%;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_table">Table 12: </span>Model architecture and training hyperparameters across all five scales.
“–” denotes not applicable.</figcaption>

<section id="A5" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix E </span>Training Loss Curves</h2>

<div id="A5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#A5.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ Appendix E Training Loss Curves ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows per-method training loss curves at four
model scales (50B tokens, 4K context).
VHA achieves the lowest convergence loss at the 4B scale and remains
competitive at 0.6B, 1.7B, and 8B-A1B, where its gap from the best-converging method is within 0.01 nats.</p>
</div>
<figure id="A5.F4" class="ltx_figure"><object type="image/svg+xml" data="2610.17959v1/loss_all_scales.svg" id="A5.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/315;" width="476" height="315"></object>
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4: </span><span id="A5.F4.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Training loss curves across four model scales.</span>
Each panel compares MHA, GQA, MLA, MFA, and VHA on FineWeb-Edu
(50B tokens, 4K context).
All curves are plotted from step 4K onward after the learning-rate warm-up;
smoothing is applied with an exponential moving average (<math id="A5.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha{=}0.93" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.93</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha{=}0.93</annotation></semantics></math>).
VHA (blue, solid) achieves the lowest loss at convergence at the 4B scale.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="A6" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix F </span>VHA Algorithm</h2>

<div id="A6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Algorithm <a href="#alg1" title="Algorithm 1 ‣ Appendix F VHA Algorithm ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> provides a self-contained reference for VHA’s training
forward pass and the one-time inference-absorption procedure that reduces the
trained model to a standard GQA-2 deployment.</p>
</div>
<figure id="alg1" class="ltx_float ltx_float_algorithm ltx_framed ltx_framed_top">

<figcaption class="ltx_caption"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_float"><span id="alg1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Algorithm 1</span> </span> Virtual Head Attention (VHA)</figcaption><div class="ltx_flex_figure">
<div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<p id="alg1.4" class="ltx_p ltx_figure_panel ltx_framed ltx_framed_topbottom"><span id="alg1.4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Training Forward Pass</span></p></div><div class="ltx_flex_break"></div><div class="ltx_flex_cell ltx_flex_size_1">
<div id="alg1.5" class="ltx_listing ltx_figure_panel ltx_listing">

</div>
<div id="alg1.l3a" class="ltx_listingline">
            <span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_listingline"><span id="alg1.l3a.1" class="ltx_text" style="font-size:80%;">3:</span></span>
            
            
           <span id="alg1.l3a.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">end</span> <span id="alg1.l3a.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">for</span>

<section id="A7" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix G </span>Premix as Structured Factorization of Virtual-Head Query Projections</h2>

<div id="A7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We show that, in the forward pass, Q Premix is mathematically equivalent to a standard multi-head attention with <math id="A7.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}=H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}=H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> virtual query heads, whose per-virtual-head query projections are constrained to a structured low-dimensional manifold. The training-time benefit of the separated parameterization arises from the coupled gradient structure induced by this factorization.</p>
</div>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{q}^{\prime}d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>phys</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times H_{q}^{\prime}d}</annotation></semantics></math> be the physical query projection (with <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> heads, each of dimension <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>d</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d</annotation></semantics></math>), and let <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> be the Premix matrix for KV group <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g\in\{1,\dots,H_{kv}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g\in\{1,\dots,H_{kv}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. For physical head <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,\dots,H_{q}^{\prime}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,\dots,H_{q}^{\prime}\}</annotation></semantics></math> within group <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math>, the virtual query is</p>

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{Q}_{i,g}\;=\;Q_{i}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\;=\;X\,W_{Q}^{(i)}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>Q</mi><mi>i</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{Q}_{i,g}\;=\;Q_{i}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\;=\;X\,W_{Q}^{(i)}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}},</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}^{(i)}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}^{(i)}\in\mathbb{R}^{h\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> is the <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th slice of <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>phys</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}}</annotation></semantics></math>. The attention output for virtual head <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(i,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(i,g)</annotation></semantics></math> is</p>

<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Forward equivalence to standard multi-head attention.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Define</p>
<table id="A7.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}\;\triangleq\;W_{Q}^{(i)}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{h\times d}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">≜</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo rspace="0.558em">∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}\;\triangleq\;W_{Q}^{(i)}\,W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\;\in\;\mathbb{R}^{h\times d}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">By the associativity of matrix multiplication, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\tilde{Q}_{i,g}=X\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\tilde{Q}_{i,g}=X\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}</annotation></semantics></math>, and therefore</p>
<table id="A7.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A7.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{head}_{i,g}\;=\;\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{X\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}K_{g}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right)V_{g}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>head</mi><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0.558em" rspace="0.558em">=</mo><mrow><mrow><mpadded style="width:3.720em;" width="3.720em"><mi>softmax</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mfrac><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>K</mi><mi>g</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msubsup></mrow><msqrt><mi>d</mi></msqrt></mfrac><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>V</mi><mi>g</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{head}_{i,g}\;=\;\mathrm{softmax}\!\left(\frac{X\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}K_{g}^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}}\right)V_{g}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">holds as a pointwise identity for every input <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>X</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">X</annotation></semantics></math> and every parameter assignment. Hence VHA is, at the level of input-output behavior, a standard multi-head attention with <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> query heads and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math> KV heads, in which the <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>i</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i</annotation></semantics></math>-th virtual head of group <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="g" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>g</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">g</annotation></semantics></math> uses the projection matrix <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">The factorization defines a low-dimensional parameter manifold.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The standard <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>-head Q projection has <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}hd=H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}hd" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}hd=H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}hd</annotation></semantics></math> free parameters. The Premix factorization uses</p>
<table id="A7.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>

</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">parameters, parameterized by <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}},\{W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\}_{g=1}^{H_{kv}})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>phys</mi></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}},\{W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\}_{g=1}^{H_{kv}})</annotation></semantics></math>. The set of attainable <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}\}</annotation></semantics></math> tuples is therefore a structured submanifold of the unconstrained parameter space:</p>
<table id="A7.E11" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
