</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.3" class="ltx_p">At the 1.7B scale (<math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="h{=}2048" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>h</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2048</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">h{=}2048</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d{=}128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>d</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d{=}128</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}^{\prime}{=}8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}^{\prime}{=}8</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}{=}2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}{=}2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}{=}16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}{=}16</annotation></semantics></math>), the factorized parameterization uses <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m10" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>2.13M parameters, compared to <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m11" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>4.19M for the unconstrained <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m12" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math>-head Q projection, a <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m13" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sim" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mo>∼</mo><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sim</annotation></semantics></math>50% reduction. The corresponding Q-projection FLOPs are reduced by a similar factor, as the additional cost <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m14" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}d^{2}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>d</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2H_{kv}H_{q}^{\prime}d^{2}</annotation></semantics></math> of applying Premix is much smaller than the savings <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m15" class="ltx_Math" alttext="2hH_{q}^{\prime}(H_{kv}-1)d" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mn>2</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">2hH_{q}^{\prime}(H_{kv}-1)d</annotation></semantics></math> achieved by halving the physical head count. This is the principal source of VHA’s reduction in training and prefill FLOPs.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reparameterization benefit via gradient coupling.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although Eq. <a href="#A7.E9" title="In Forward equivalence to standard multi-head attention. ‣ Appendix G Premix as Structured Factorization of Virtual-Head Query Projections ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> shows that the forward pass is algebraically equivalent to training a single matrix <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}</annotation></semantics></math> per virtual head, the gradients under the factorized parameterization are coupled across groups and physical heads:</p>
<table id="A7.EGx1" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A7.E12"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A7.E12.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial W_{Q}^{(i)}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial W_{Q}^{(i)}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A7.E12.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\sum_{g=1}^{H_{kv}}X^{\top}\,\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial\tilde{Q}_{i,g}}\,\big(W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\big)^{\top}," display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><mstyle displaystyle="true"><munderover><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub></munderover></mstyle><mrow><msup><mi>X</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msub><mover accent="true"><mi>Q</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\sum_{g=1}^{H_{kv}}X^{\top}\,\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial\tilde{Q}_{i,g}}\,\big(W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\big)^{\top},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(12)</span></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A7.E13"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A7.E13.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mstyle displaystyle="true"><mfrac><mrow><mo>∂</mo><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℒ</mi></mrow><mrow><mo>∂</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow></mfrac></mstyle><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}}{\partial W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}}</annotation></semantics></math></td>

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(13)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Each <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math> aggregates contributions from all <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}</annotation></semantics></math> groups, modulated by the corresponding Premix matrices, while each <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math> receives gradient signal through all <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{q}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>H</mi><mi>q</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{q}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> physical heads. SGD on the factorized parameters therefore traverses the manifold <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{M}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">ℳ</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{M}</annotation></semantics></math> along directions induced by this coupled gradient structure, which differs from the trajectories obtained by independently optimizing <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px4.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> unconstrained virtual-head matrices. This is the same source of implicit regularization that underlies LoRA <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib19" title="" class="ltx_ref">Hu et al., 2022</a>]</cite> and RepVGG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ding et al., 2021</a>]</cite>: a forward-equivalent factorization of a large weight tensor yields different optimization dynamics and, empirically, different (and often better) final solutions.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Inference-time absorption.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Since the forward equivalence in Eq. <a href="#A7.E9" title="In Forward equivalence to standard multi-head attention. ‣ Appendix G Premix as Structured Factorization of Virtual-Head Query Projections ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">9</span></a> holds for any frozen parameter values, at inference we simply precompute <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math> for all <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(i,g)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(i,g)</annotation></semantics></math> pairs and discard <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mi>phys</mi></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{Q}^{\mathrm{phys}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}\}</annotation></semantics></math>. The model then runs as a standard GQA-2 with <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> independent query projections, <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{kv}=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{kv}=2</annotation></semantics></math> KV heads, and the same output projection <math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px5.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, fully compatible with existing GQA serving kernels.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px6" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Unified view with Postmix.</h4>

<div id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Premix and Postmix are two instantiations of the same head-axis reparameterization principle. Premix factorizes the per-virtual-head query projection on the Q side (<math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mover accent="true"><mi>W</mi><mo>~</mo></mover><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>g</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>Q</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>g</mi><mi>premix</mi></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\widetilde{W}_{Q}^{(i,g)}=W_{Q}^{(i)}W_{g}^{\mathrm{premix}}</annotation></semantics></math>); Postmix factorizes the merged output projection on the O side (<math id="A7.SS0.SSS0.Px6.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, see Appendix <a href="#A8" title="Appendix H Proof of Postmix Linear Redundancy ‣ Virtual Head Attention" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">H</span></a>). Both are forward-equivalent to a standard GQA in their merged form, both gain training-time benefits from coupled gradients of the separated parameters, and both fold back into a standard GQA-2 architecture at inference with zero overhead.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="A8" class="ltx_appendix">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_appendix"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_appendix">Appendix H </span>Proof of Postmix Linear Redundancy</h2>

<div id="A8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We prove that Linear Postmix can be mathematically absorbed into the output projection <math id="A8.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math>, and discuss why the separated parameterization nonetheless improves training.</p>
</div>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Setup.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">For a single token, let <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times d}</annotation></semantics></math> be the concatenated attention output across all <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> virtual heads. Postmix computes:</p>
<table id="A8.E14" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E14.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y^{\prime}=(I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top})\,Y" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y^{\prime}=(I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top})\,Y</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(14)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times r}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A,B\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times r}</annotation></semantics></math>. The final output is obtained by applying the output projection:</p>
<table id="A8.E15" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E15.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{output}^{\top}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y^{\prime})^{\top}W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times h}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>output</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{output}^{\top}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y^{\prime})^{\top}W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{1\times h}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(15)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.3" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(\cdot)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">⋅</mo><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(\cdot)</annotation></semantics></math> flattens a matrix in row-major order (i.e., <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\mathrm{.reshape}(H_{v}d)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0.167em">.</mo><mrow><mi>reshape</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\mathrm{.reshape}(H_{v}d)</annotation></semantics></math> in PyTorch, concatenating head outputs).</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Absorption via Kronecker product.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Using the row-major identity: for <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times H_{v}}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times H_{v}}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Y</mi><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}\times d}</annotation></semantics></math>,</p>
<table id="A8.E16" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="A8.E16.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(MY)^{\top}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\bigl(M^{\top}\otimes I_{d}\bigr)" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(MY)^{\top}=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\bigl(M^{\top}\otimes I_{d}\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(16)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Setting <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M=I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>M</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M=I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> (so <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="M^{\top}=I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>M</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">M^{\top}=I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Roger and Charles, 1994</a>]</cite>:</p>
<table id="A8.EGx2" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A8.Ex1"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y^{\prime})^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y^{\prime})^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.Ex1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}\!\left((I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top})\,Y\right)^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}\!\left((I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top})\,Y\right)^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A8.E17"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.E17.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(17)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Substituting into the output computation:</p>
<table id="A8.EGx3" class="ltx_equationgroup ltx_eqn_align ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody id="A8.Ex2"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_right ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle\mathrm{output}^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msup><mi>output</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle\mathrm{output}^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.Ex2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y^{\prime})^{\top}W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y^{\prime})^{\top}W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A8.Ex3"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
<tbody id="A8.E18"><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_eqn_cell"></td>
<td class="ltx_td ltx_align_left ltx_eqn_cell"><math id="A8.E18.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}W_{O}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mphantom></mphantom><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>vec</mi><mtext>row</mtext></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>Y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>⊤</mo></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\displaystyle=\mathrm{vec}_{\text{row}}(Y)^{\top}W_{O}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(18)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.055em" stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo rspace="0.222em">⊗</mo><msub><mi>I</mi><mi>d</mi></msub></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub></mrow><mo>∈</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><mi>h</mi></mrow></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}^{\prime}=\bigl((I_{H_{v}}+AB^{\top})\otimes I_{d}\bigr)W_{O}\in\mathbb{R}^{H_{v}d\times h}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Since <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>I</mi><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></msub><mo>+</mo><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">I_{H_{v}}+BA^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math> is generically invertible (it equals the identity at initialization and remains near-identity during training), <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> has the same number of free parameters as <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math>. Therefore, for any choice of <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O},A,B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O},A,B</annotation></semantics></math>, there exists a single matrix <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> that produces the identical output, confirming that Postmix is theoretically redundant.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Reparameterization benefit.</h4>

<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Despite this redundancy, the separated parameterization <math id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\{W_{O},A,B\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><mi>A</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>B</mi><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\{W_{O},A,B\}</annotation></semantics></math> provides training advantages analogous to those observed in RepVGG <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">[<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ding et al., 2021</a>]</cite>:</p>
</div>
<div id="A8.SS0.SSS0.Px3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="A8.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="A8.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="A8.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Factored gradient paths.</span> The gradients with respect to <math id="A8.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="A" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>A</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">A</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="A8.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="A8.I1.i1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}</annotation></semantics></math> follow different paths through the computation graph. This factorization provides a form of implicit regularization, as the effective weight update to <math id="A8.I1.i1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="W_{O}^{\prime}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>W</mi><mi>O</mi><mo>′</mo></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">W_{O}^{\prime}</annotation></semantics></math> at each step is constrained by the low-rank structure of <math id="A8.I1.i1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="AB^{\top}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>A</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>B</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">AB^{\top}</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A8.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="A8.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Identity initialization.</span> With <math id="A8.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>B</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B</annotation></semantics></math> initialized to zero, <math id="A8.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="BA^{\top}=0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi>B</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msup><mi>A</mi><mo>⊤</mo></msup></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">BA^{\top}=0</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="A8.I1.i2.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Y^{\prime}=Y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msup><mi>Y</mi><mo>′</mo></msup><mo>=</mo><mi>Y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Y^{\prime}=Y</annotation></semantics></math> at the start of training. Postmix begins as a no-op and gradually learns useful cross-group mixing patterns, avoiding disruption to the early training dynamics.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="A8.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="A8.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="A8.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="A8.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Low-rank constraint.</span> The bottleneck rank <math id="A8.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r\ll H_{v}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>≪</mo><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>v</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r\ll H_{v}</annotation></semantics></math> limits the expressiveness of the cross-head mixing, acting as a structural regularizer. This prevents Postmix from overfitting, consistent with the ablation finding that larger ranks (<math id="A8.I1.i3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="r{=}32,128" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>32,128</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">r{=}32,128</annotation></semantics></math>) degrade evaluation performance despite lower training loss.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
</section>
</article>
